header.contentArea: Perioperative care: venous thromboembolism prophylaxis (management viva)
guidelineVersions: NICE NG89 Venous thromboembolism in over 16s (published 21 March 2018, last updated 13 August 2019)
Association of Anaesthetists, OAA and RA-UK: Regional anaesthesia and patients with abnormalities of coagulation (Anaesthesia, September 2013)

related.why: Stopping and restarting therapeutic anticoagulants around surgery
Taking the history when a postoperative DVT is suspected
Suspected epidural haematoma: the complication that LMWH and epidural timing aim to prevent

brief.role: Core surgical trainee on the general surgical team
brief.scenario: Mr Oyelaran, 68, had an emergency laparotomy and Hartmann's procedure for perforated sigmoid diverticulitis 18 hours ago. He has a thoracic epidural. His BMI is 33. He had a DVT after a knee replacement 6 years ago and takes no anticoagulant. The nurse points out that no VTE prophylaxis has been prescribed since admission.
brief.task: Discuss his VTE prophylaxis with the examiner.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Weigh VTE risk against bleeding risk, then time the LMWH around the epidural.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Prescribing LMWH without thinking about the epidural catheter, or waiting until he mobilises.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "He's high VTE risk and prophylaxis is overdue. I'd check his bleeding risk now."

grid.label: Assesses VTE and bleeding risk
grid.fail: Prescribes by habit without assessing either risk.
grid.pass: Assesses VTE and bleeding risk with a national tool, such as the Department of Health tool; reassesses at consultant review or clinical change.
grid.high: Names his VTE risks (age, major emergency surgery, obesity, previous DVT, immobility) and bleeding risks (fresh surgery, epidural catheter).

grid.label: Addresses the missed prophylaxis
grid.fail: Ignores the omission or leaves it for the day team.
grid.pass: Recognises prophylaxis should start within 14 hours of the decision to admit; prescribes now if bleeding risk allows.
grid.high: Informs the consultant, reports it as a patient safety incident, and explains the omission honestly to the patient.

grid.label: Checks bleeding risk before LMWH
grid.fail: Starts LMWH without checking for bleeding, platelets or renal function.
grid.pass: Checks drain, stoma and wound for bleeding, and haemoglobin, platelets, clotting and eGFR.
grid.high: Holds LMWH while actively bleeding and relies on mechanical methods; with severe renal impairment uses reduced-dose LMWH or unfractionated heparin.

grid.label: Mechanical prophylaxis
grid.fail: Fits stockings without checking for contraindications.
grid.pass: Anti-embolism stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression from admission until his mobility is back to normal.
grid.high: Checks for peripheral arterial disease, neuropathy, severe oedema or fragile skin; uses intermittent compression where stockings are contraindicated.

grid.label: Pharmacological agent and duration
grid.fail: Chooses aspirin, or stops prophylaxis at discharge whatever the day.
grid.pass: LMWH, or fondaparinux, for a minimum of 7 days, continuing after discharge if needed.
grid.high: Would consider extending to 28 days if histology shows cancer; teaches self-injection and informs the GP.

grid.label: Times LMWH around the epidural
grid.fail: Gives LMWH without considering the epidural catheter.
grid.pass: Agrees timing with the anaesthetist: catheter removed at least 12 hours after a prophylactic LMWH dose.
grid.high: Next dose no sooner than 4 hours after removal; monitors for back pain and new leg weakness or numbness.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you decide on his VTE prophylaxis?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Everyone after a laparotomy gets LMWH, so I'd just write it up.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: It should have been started already.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That's the admitting team's problem. I'd leave it for the day team to sort out.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Anything to check before you prescribe?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd ask the nurses to put them on.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What drug and for how long?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That doesn't affect anything, I'd give the LMWH tonight.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How would you decide on his VTE prophylaxis?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'd assess his VTE and bleeding risk with a national tool such as the Department of Health one, and reassess at consultant review or if things change.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It should have started within 14 hours of the decision to admit. I'd prescribe it now if his bleeding risk allows.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The drain, stoma and wound for bleeding, and his haemoglobin, platelets, clotting and eGFR.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression, continued until his mobility is back to normal.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Which drug, and for how long?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: LMWH, or fondaparinux, for at least 7 days, continued after discharge if needed.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'd agree timing with the anaesthetist. The catheter must come out at least 12 hours after a prophylactic dose.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: High. He's older, obese, had major emergency surgery, is immobile and has had a DVT. His bleeding risks are fresh surgery and the epidural catheter.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: It should have been started already.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Yes. I'd prescribe it now, tell my consultant, report it as a patient safety incident and explain the omission to him honestly.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: His drain has 400 mL of fresh blood overnight.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Then he may be bleeding, so I'd hold LMWH, rely on mechanical prophylaxis and get a senior review. If his eGFR were below 30, I'd use a reduced LMWH dose or unfractionated heparin.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: He has absent foot pulses and claudication.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No stockings with peripheral arterial disease. I'd use intermittent pneumatic compression instead.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Then I'd consider extending LMWH to 28 days. I'd teach him to self-inject and let his GP know.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The anaesthetist wants to remove the epidural two hours after this evening's dose.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd ask them to wait until 12 hours after the dose, and give the next dose no sooner than 4 hours after removal. The nurses should report back pain or new leg weakness or numbness at once.

failures.move: Giving LMWH without coordinating its timing with epidural catheter removal.
failures.consequence: Risks a vertebral canal haematoma and permanent paralysis.

failures.move: Starting LMWH without checking for active bleeding or renal function.
failures.consequence: Can worsen postoperative haemorrhage or accumulate in renal impairment.

failures.move: Leaving the missed prophylaxis for someone else.
failures.consequence: A high-risk patient goes longer unprotected; the system failure is not learned from.

failures.move: Fitting stockings to a patient with peripheral arterial disease.
failures.consequence: Can cause skin necrosis and limb ischaemia.

recovery.line: Before the first dose, I'd agree timing with the anaesthetist so the catheter comes out at least 12 hours after it.
Start as soon as possible, within 14 hours of the decision to admit, once bleeding risk allows.

knowledge.fact: Assess VTE and bleeding risk on admission or by first consultant review; reassess at consultant review or with clinical change.
Start pharmacological prophylaxis as soon as possible and within 14 hours of the decision to admit.

Abdominal surgery: mechanical prophylaxis from admission until mobility is normal; add LMWH or fondaparinux for at least 7 days if VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk; consider 28 days after major abdominal cancer surgery.
No stockings with peripheral arterial disease or bypass, neuropathy, severe oedema or fragile skin.
Remove an epidural catheter at least 12 hours after prophylactic LMWH; give the next dose at least 4 hours after removal.

recall.think: PE after surgery; epidural haematoma from badly timed LMWH.
recall.say: "High VTE risk, prophylaxis overdue: start now if not bleeding."

numbers.meaning: latest start after decision to admit
dose to catheter removal; removal to next dose

recall.finish: LMWH at least 7 days with mechanical prophylaxis.

sources.name: NICE guideline NG89: Venous thromboembolism in over 16s: reducing the risk of hospital-acquired deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
sources.supports: Risk assessment with a national tool and reassessment (1.1.5–1.1.8); start within 14 hours of decision to admit (1.1.7); stocking contraindications (1.3.1); LMWH or UFH in renal impairment, eGFR below 30 (1.5.1–1.5.2); abdominal surgery: mechanical from admission, LMWH or fondaparinux for at least 7 days, consider 28 days after major abdominal cancer surgery (1.14.2–1.14.4); discharge information and GP notification (1.2.5, 1.2.8)

sources.name: Harrop-Griffiths W, et al. Regional anaesthesia and patients with abnormalities of coagulation (Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain & Ireland, Obstetric Anaesthetists' Association, Regional Anaesthesia UK). Anaesthesia 2013;68(9):966–72
sources.supports: Prophylactic LMWH: 12 hours from last dose to neuraxial block or catheter removal; 4 hours from removal to next dose

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format: 9 minutes with 1 minute's reading; examiner-led questioning in applied knowledge stations

partner.opening: This man is 18 hours after an emergency Hartmann's. Nobody has prescribed VTE prophylaxis. What would you do?

reveals.finding: Drain 60 mL serosanguinous since theatre. Stoma pink, no bleeding. Wound dry.
Hb 121 g/L, platelets 238 x10^9/L, INR 1.1, eGFR 74 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Foot pulses present, no oedema, skin intact.
Thoracic epidural running well; the anaesthetists plan to remove it tomorrow.

push.question: When should prophylaxis have started?
push.expect: Within 14 hours of the decision to admit.

push.question: Which drug, and for how long?
push.expect: LMWH or fondaparinux for at least 7 days.

push.question: How does the epidural change things?
push.expect: Removal at least 12 hours after a dose; next dose at least 4 hours after removal.

curveballs.prompt: His drain has 400 mL of fresh blood overnight.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Hold LMWH, mechanical prophylaxis only, senior review for bleeding.

curveballs.prompt: He has absent foot pulses and claudication.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Consider extending LMWH to 28 days after surgery.

curveballs.prompt: The anaesthetist wants to pull the epidural two hours after tonight's LMWH.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Wait until 12 hours after the dose; next dose at least 4 hours after removal.
